subject: Invoice tranche sweep and cost-map reconciliation
messages:
From: Mara Patel <mara.patel@greenlinelogistics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-entity disbursement: weekly tranche sweep inquiry

Hi Hannah,

Quick intro — I’m Mara in Finance at GreenLine. We ran into a wrinkle while preparing April invoices: our customers are billed centrally but remits need to be sliced across three GreenLine legal entities (GL-US, GL-EU, GL-AP). Historically we do a manual sweep each week to route cash and attach VAT tags per entity.

Before we start a pilot with Redwood, two asks:
- Can Redwood emit split invoices (single customer invoice with multiple remit rows) and return accounting-level ledger references for automated pairing?
- We’d like a weekly tranche sweep (every Monday) where funds received are allocated to entities based on the attached cost allocation map. Can you confirm workflow and timing?

I’ve attached a short CSV of current remit rules (redacted) for context. If this looks feasible we’ll escalate to procurement for terms/POs.

Thanks — hope to sync soon.

Mara Patel
Director, Finance Operations
GreenLine Logistics
attachments: GL_remit_sample.csv
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Mara Patel <mara.patel@greenlinelogistics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-entity disbursement: weekly tranche sweep inquiry

Hi Mara — thanks for the clear note and sample. We can support what you described but want to confirm a couple of operational details before we propose the sweep cadence and mapping format.

High-level plan:
- Redwood can emit a single PDF invoice with multiple remit rows (split-row). Each remit row will include an entity tag and a ledger reference (entity_id + cost_center).
- We can surface a ledger pairing field in the webhook/GL export so your AP system can auto-pair receipts.
- For the weekly sweep: Redwood can schedule a "tranche settlement" job that produces a settlement file (CSV) every Monday 02:00 UTC and triggers a webhook to your collection endpoint.

What we need from you:
1) A finalized cost allocation map (entity -> cost center -> percentage) — I’ve attached a costmap template and a short mutual action plan to outline milestones.
2) Tax jurisdiction matrix per legal entity (VAT rates / reverse-charge flags).

I’ve looped in Kim (accounting) and Ben (payments infra) to confirm ledger formats and whether we should use an automated remit-sweep or a manual review gate for the first two runs.

Next steps: can you send the cost allocation map and jurisdiction table by EOD Friday? If so we’ll produce a PoC settlement file and a stubbed webhook for testing.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Finance GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: costmap_template.xlsx, mutual_action_plan.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Mara Patel <mara.patel@greenlinelogistics.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-entity disbursement: weekly tranche sweep inquiry

Thanks Hannah — quick accounting note.

Kimberly here. We reviewed the sample remit rules Mara shared. From an internal ledger perspective we need the settlement file to include these columns (required):
- invoice_id, invoice_date, remit_row_id, amount, currency, entity_code, ledger_account, cost_center, vat_rate, vat_amount, allocation_pct, original_customer_id

If the remit_row includes entity_code we can auto-post to the right AR sub-ledger. For VAT: please include a per-row VAT flag (reverse_charge=true/false) and a jurisdiction_code.

Proposed interim mapping:
- GL-US -> ledger 4100, cost_center 700-US
- GL-EU -> ledger 4110, cost_center 700-EU
- GL-AP -> ledger 4120, cost_center 700-AP

I attached a quick CSV with the mapping we plan to use for the PoC. We’ll expect Redwood to honor allocation_pct when building remit rows; rounding rules should be documented in the PoC output.

On the manual review gate: recommend the first two sweeps be manual — finance will validate totals and VAT tags before we flip to automated. After two successful runs we can enable automated weekly sweeps.

--
Kimberly Park
Manager, Revenue Accounting
Redwood Inference
attachments: entity_mapping_v1.csv

Adding payments infra context. We can implement the tranche sweep as a scheduled job that emits a signed settlement CSV and POSTs to GreenLine's collection endpoint. Implementation notes:
- Initial mode: "manual approve" — settlement file posted to a staging endpoint and to a Slack channel + finance dashboard (PDF + CSV) for sign-off.
- After two approved runs, flip to "auto-post" to production endpoint.
- We will include a header HMAC and timestamp, and publish a change-log for rounding adjustments.

Estimated timeline once we have the costmap + VAT matrix:
- Day 0-2: map validation + build PoC output
- Day 3-4: sandbox webhook + two staged sweeps
- Day 5: enable automation (if sign-off obtained)

Action items (internal + to Mara):
- Hannah/Kim: confirm rounding policy and sign-off on mapping.
- Mara: provide cost allocation map and VAT matrix by EOD Friday.
- Ben: will kick off PoC after we receive artifacts.

Thanks — I’ll draft the small SOW paragraph to append to the PoC for procurement.

Ben Carter
Lead, Payments Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
